info.title: Split the problem
info.text:
Start with the whole task.

Identify separate responsibilities.

Break large parts down further.

Challenge: Suggest three parts of a library system.

Manage members, issue books and process returned books are suitable parts.

info.title: Read the hierarchy
info.text:
The top box is the whole system.

Child boxes are parts of their parent.

Lower levels show more detail.

Challenge: What are the two parts of Issue loan?

Check availability and record borrower.

info.title: Refine a sub-problem
info.text:
Refinement adds useful detail.

Stop when each task is clear enough to solve.

Keep the hierarchy logically grouped.

Challenge: Break Process return into three smaller tasks.

Find the active loan, mark it returned and make the item available again.

info.title: Structure versus flow
info.text:
Structure diagrams show parts.

Flowcharts show execution and decisions.

A hierarchy does not specify run order.

Challenge: Why is a structure diagram not a flowchart?

It shows what the system contains, rather than the order of execution and decision paths.

info.title: Work as a team
info.text:
Smaller tasks can be allocated to people.

Parts can be tested separately.

Interfaces between parts must still agree.

Challenge: Why must both programmers agree on member ID?

Their parts exchange member details. A consistent ID allows the parts to work together.

info.title: Check coverage
info.text:
Compare the parts with the requirements.

Look for missing responsibilities.

Avoid duplicate or unclear tasks.

Challenge: Which responsibility is missing?

Processing returns is missing and must be included.
